findings.title: Calibration pulse
findings.explanation: The pulse is 1 mV tall and 200 ms wide. Check speed and gain before counting boxes.

findings.title: P wave and PR interval
findings.explanation: P is atrial depolarization. Measure PR from the beginning of P to the beginning of QRS, including the P wave.

findings.title: QRS and ST segment
findings.explanation: QRS is ventricular depolarization. The ST segment begins at the end of QRS (the J point); compare it with the isoelectric baseline.

findings.title: T wave and QT interval
findings.explanation: T is ventricular repolarization. QT runs from QRS onset to T end; QTc also accounts for heart rate.

findings.title: R–R and rate
findings.explanation: In this regular rhythm, four large boxes between R peaks gives 300 ÷ 4 = 75/min at 25 mm/s. Use a longer strip for irregular rhythms.

findings.title: Sinus P and narrow QRS
findings.explanation: The upper strip has a P before each QRS with a consistent PR. Inspect P-wave direction in the appropriate leads before naming sinus rhythm.

findings.title: Wide QRS
findings.explanation: The middle strip has wider ventricular complexes. Width alone cannot distinguish VT from supraventricular conduction with aberrancy.

findings.title: Irregular R–R intervals
findings.explanation: Compare successive R peaks in the lower strip: the intervals vary and there is no organized repeating P wave.

findings.title: Axis quadrants
findings.explanation: Use the net QRS direction in I and aVF. If I is positive and aVF negative, lead II helps distinguish a normal leftward axis from left-axis deviation.

V5 · R wave at half gain

findings.title: Deep S in V1
findings.explanation: This voltage panel is drawn at half gain (5 mm/mV). The displayed S depth corresponds to 15 mm at standard gain.

findings.title: Tall R in V5
findings.explanation: The displayed R height corresponds to 22 mm at standard gain. Combine the appropriate voltages only after correcting for gain; voltage criteria alone do not establish anatomic hypertrophy.

findings.title: Low-voltage example
findings.explanation: The lower strip illustrates small complexes. Whole-ECG low voltage requires the relevant lead set, not just this single strip.

omi-equivalents.title: OMI equivalents at a glance
omi-equivalents.caption: Synthetic focused examples of hyperacute T waves, de Winter morphology and Wellens type B. Lead II below is a normal rhythm reference. These are separate teaching examples, not one patient ECG.

findings.title: Hyperacute T morphology
findings.explanation: The left example emphasizes a broad, bulky T wave relative to QRS. Assess territory, symptoms and serial change on a complete ECG.

findings.title: de Winter morphology
findings.explanation: The middle example combines an upsloping depressed ST segment and a tall T wave. Read the ST–T shape together.

findings.title: Wellens-type inversion
findings.explanation: The right example shows a deep inverted anterior T wave. Interpret with the recent angina history and clinical setting.

findings.title: Separate normal rhythm reference
findings.explanation: Lead II below is a normal rhythm reference. The three upper examples are separate teaching patterns, not simultaneous leads from one patient.

toxic-metabolic-mimics.title: Bizarre = metabolic/toxic
toxic-metabolic-mimics.caption: Synthetic focused leads, not a patient recording or a full 12-lead. Each small box represents 40 ms / 0.1 mV at this setting. Three possible hyperkalemia appearances, not a predictable sequence or potassium-level scale.

findings.title: Peaked T appearance
findings.explanation: A narrow peaked T wave may occur with hyperkalemia. A normal ECG does not exclude dangerous hyperkalemia.

findings.title: P / PR / QRS changes
findings.explanation: This example combines attenuated P waves, delayed AV conduction and QRS widening. These changes need not occur in a fixed sequence.

findings.title: Fused QRS–T appearance
findings.explanation: The sine-wave example has no discrete P, QRS or T endpoints to measure. These variants do not predict a potassium concentration.

stemi-criteria.title: Inferior STEMI pattern — II, III, aVF with aVL mirror
stemi-criteria.caption: Synthetic focused leads, not a patient recording or a full 12-lead. Each small box represents 40 ms / 0.1 mV at this setting. Convex STE II + III + aVF with mirror STD in aVL — territorial STE + mirror STD supports acute inferior occlusion.

traceSpec.note: Convex STE II + III + aVF with mirror STD in aVL — territorial STE + mirror STD supports acute inferior occlusion.

findings.title: Inferior ST elevation
findings.explanation: Inspect the J point and ST segment in the contiguous inferior leads.

findings.title: Reciprocal ST depression
findings.explanation: Opposite ST displacement in aVL supports inferior ischemic injury in a compatible clinical presentation.

hyperacute-t.title: Hyperacute T — normal vs hyperacute vs hyperK
hyperacute-t.caption: Synthetic focused leads, not a patient recording or a full 12-lead. Each small box represents 40 ms / 0.1 mV at this setting. Same V3 viewpoint, three T shapes: normal vs hyperacute vs hyperK tenting.

traceSpec.note: Same V3 viewpoint, three T shapes: normal vs hyperacute vs hyperK tenting.

findings.title: Normal T comparison
findings.explanation: The normal V3 comparison has an asymmetric T wave with a smaller amplitude than R. Compare it with the two abnormal shapes below.

findings.title: Broad, bulky T wave
findings.explanation: This V3 shape comparison illustrates T-wave bulk. A single lead cannot establish the territorial distribution required in clinical interpretation.

findings.title: Narrow peaked T comparison
findings.explanation: A narrow peak is a potassium clue, not a potassium measurement. ECG appearances overlap; assess the whole tracing and laboratory results.

wellens.title: Wellens syndrome — Type A vs Type B
wellens.caption: Synthetic focused leads, not a patient recording or a full 12-lead. Each small box represents 40 ms / 0.1 mV at this setting. Pain-free interval after resolved angina: Type A biphasic (+/−) vs Type B deep symmetric inversion in V2–V3. Strongly associated with critical LAD disease in the appropriate clinical setting.

traceSpec.note: Pain-free interval after resolved angina: Type A biphasic (+/−) vs Type B deep symmetric inversion in V2–V3. Strongly associated with critical LAD disease in the appropriate clinical setting.

findings.title: Anterior T-wave abnormality
findings.explanation: Type A is initially positive then negative; Type B is deeply inverted. Interpret after recent angina, often while pain-free. The ECG pattern alone does not prove a specific coronary lesion.

findings.title: Preserved anterior R waves
findings.explanation: Preserved R waves and little ST displacement accompany this synthetic example. Clinical Wellens assessment also requires the history and exclusion of mimics.

dewinter.title: de Winter pattern — precordial STD with tall T waves
dewinter.caption: Synthetic focused leads, not a patient recording or a full 12-lead. Each small box represents 40 ms / 0.1 mV at this setting. Upsloping J-point ST depression with tall symmetric T waves across V2–V6. aVR elevation is supportive and may be absent.

traceSpec.note: Upsloping J-point ST depression with tall symmetric T waves across V2–V6. aVR elevation is supportive and may be absent.

findings.title: Upsloping ST depression
findings.explanation: The depressed J point rises toward tall T waves across the precordial leads. This is a high-risk occlusion pattern in the right clinical context.

findings.title: Tall symmetric T waves
findings.explanation: Inspect the ST segment together with the prominent T wave; tall T amplitude alone is nonspecific.

findings.title: Associated aVR elevation
findings.explanation: aVR elevation can accompany de Winter morphology; it is neither required nor independently diagnostic.

sgarbossa.title: Smith-modified Sgarbossa positive
sgarbossa.caption: Synthetic focused leads, not a patient recording or a full 12-lead. Each small box represents 40 ms / 0.1 mV at this setting. LBBB-like wide complexes: concordant anterior ST depression and concordant lateral STE are abnormal.

traceSpec.note: LBBB-like wide complexes: concordant anterior ST depression and concordant lateral STE are abnormal.

findings.title: Concordant elevation
findings.explanation: ST elevation follows the positive QRS direction.

findings.title: Concordant depression
findings.explanation: ST depression follows a negative QRS in an anterior lead.

findings.title: Excessive discordance
findings.explanation: Compare J-point elevation with S-wave depth. Modified Sgarbossa supports occlusion assessment in LBBB or ventricular pacing; clinical context remains essential.

posterior-omi.title: Posterior OMI mirror pattern
posterior-omi.caption: Synthetic focused leads, not a patient recording or a full 12-lead. Each small box represents 40 ms / 0.1 mV at this setting. V1–V3 horizontal ST depression with dominant R and upright T raises concern for posterior occlusion. Record V7–V9 and interpret clinically.

traceSpec.note: V1–V3 horizontal ST depression with dominant R and upright T raises concern for posterior occlusion. Record V7–V9 and interpret clinically.

findings.title: Anterior mirror depression
findings.explanation: Horizontal ST depression in V1–V3 raises concern for posterior injury.

findings.title: Prominent R and upright T
findings.explanation: These accompanying features support the posterior mirror pattern but may be absent early.

findings.title: Posterior lead elevation
findings.explanation: V7–V9 show contiguous posterior elevation of 1.0, 0.8 and 0.6 mm. The usual posterior threshold is 0.5 mm; 1 mm is used for greater specificity in men under 40. Interpret with symptoms and serial changes; negative posterior leads do not exclude occlusion.

avr-lmca.title: aVR elevation with diffuse ST depression
avr-lmca.caption: Synthetic educational strip · 6 seconds · selected leads, not a full 12-lead. Grid and waveform share a calibrated scale; on-screen millimetres depend on zoom. Selected morphology, not a clinically validated patient ECG.

findings.title: Widespread ST depression
findings.explanation: Horizontal ST depression is present in the displayed limb and lateral chest leads. Assess the distribution on a complete ECG and compare serial changes.

findings.title: Opposite aVR elevation
findings.explanation: The aVR ST segment is elevated while several other leads are depressed. This indicates global subendocardial ischemia in context; it cannot identify a left-main lesion.

findings.title: Interpret perfusion and symptoms
findings.explanation: Consider ACS as well as severe supply–demand imbalance. Ongoing ischemia or hemodynamic compromise needs urgent assessment; this pattern is not an automatic STEMI diagnosis.

hyperkalemia.title: Severe hyperkalaemia pattern
hyperkalemia.caption: Synthetic focused leads, not a patient recording or a full 12-lead. Each small box represents 40 ms / 0.1 mV at this setting. Three possible hyperkalemia appearances, not a predictable sequence or potassium-level scale.

traceSpec.note: Three possible hyperkalemia appearances, not a predictable sequence or potassium-level scale.

findings.title: Peaked T appearance
findings.explanation: A narrow peaked T wave may occur with hyperkalemia. A normal ECG does not exclude dangerous hyperkalemia.

findings.title: P / PR / QRS changes
findings.explanation: This example combines attenuated P waves, delayed AV conduction and QRS widening. These changes need not occur in a fixed sequence.

findings.title: Fused QRS–T appearance
findings.explanation: The sine-wave example has no discrete P, QRS or T endpoints to measure. These variants do not predict a potassium concentration.

hypokalemia.title: Hypokalaemia with U waves
hypokalemia.caption: Synthetic educational strip · 6 seconds · selected leads, not a full 12-lead. Grid and waveform share a calibrated scale; on-screen millimetres depend on zoom. Selected morphology, not a clinically validated patient ECG.

findings.title: Depressed ST and flattened T
findings.explanation: The ST lies below the TP baseline and the T wave is small. ECG appearances cannot determine the potassium concentration or exclude hypokalemia.

findings.title: U follows the completed T
findings.explanation: A separate positive U follows T. This model ends T at 380 ms and U at 620 ms after QRS onset; U must not be counted as part of QT.

findings.title: QT versus QU
findings.explanation: Measure QRS onset to T end, not to U end. When T and U merge clinically, use another lead with a clear endpoint rather than reporting a falsely precise QT.

hypothermia.title: Hypothermia with Osborn waves
hypothermia.caption: Synthetic educational strip · 6 seconds · selected leads, not a full 12-lead. Grid and waveform share a calibrated scale; on-screen millimetres depend on zoom. Selected morphology, not a clinically validated patient ECG.

findings.title: Sinus bradycardia at 40/min
findings.explanation: Each QRS is preceded by P; the R–R interval is 1,500 ms. Hypothermia may also cause atrial fibrillation and other arrhythmias.

findings.title: J wave at the QRS–ST junction
findings.explanation: A rounded Osborn hump follows the terminal QRS. J waves are compatible with hypothermia but are not specific for it and do not measure core temperature.

findings.title: Prolonged conduction and repolarization
findings.explanation: This model has PR 240 ms, QRS 120 ms and QT 560 ms. QT is the uncorrected interval; evaluate core temperature and the patient.

brugada.title: Brugada type 1 pattern
brugada.caption: Synthetic educational strip · 6 seconds · selected leads, not a full 12-lead. Grid and waveform share a calibrated scale; on-screen millimetres depend on zoom. Selected morphology, not a clinically validated patient ECG.

findings.title: Coved right-precordial elevation
findings.explanation: The J/ST junction is elevated 3 mm in V1 and 2.5 mm in V2 at standard gain, descending in a coved contour. Type 1 morphology requires at least 2 mm in at least one of V1 or V2.

findings.title: Negative T after the cove
findings.explanation: Follow the elevated ST continuously into an inverted T wave. A saddleback appearance alone is not the diagnostic type 1 pattern.

findings.title: Pattern versus syndrome
findings.explanation: Use V1/V2 in the second, third or fourth intercostal spaces when clinically indicated. Assess fever, drugs, symptoms, family history and phenocopies; this synthetic pattern alone does not establish Brugada syndrome.

pe-strain.title: Pulmonary embolism strain pattern
pe-strain.caption: Synthetic educational strip · 6 seconds · selected leads, not a full 12-lead. Grid and waveform share a calibrated scale; on-screen millimetres depend on zoom. Selected morphology, not a clinically validated patient ECG.

findings.title: Sinus tachycardia
findings.explanation: The sinus rate is 110/min with a P before each QRS. Tachycardia is common in PE but highly nonspecific.

findings.title: S in I; Q and inverted T in III
findings.explanation: Read the deep terminal S in I with the initial Q and negative T in III. S1Q3T3 is a right-heart strain clue, not a diagnosis of PE.

findings.title: Anterior T-wave inversion
findings.explanation: Negative T waves in V1–V4 support right ventricular strain in context. Similar changes have other causes; a normal ECG cannot exclude PE.

pericarditis-ber.title: Acute pericarditis pattern
pericarditis-ber.caption: Synthetic educational strip · 6 seconds · selected leads, not a full 12-lead. Grid and waveform share a calibrated scale; on-screen millimetres depend on zoom. Selected morphology, not a clinically validated patient ECG.

findings.title: ST elevation across lead territories
findings.explanation: The displayed limb and lateral chest leads have upward-concave ST elevation. Confirm widespread involvement on the full ECG; concavity alone cannot exclude coronary occlusion.

findings.title: PR depression relative to TP
findings.explanation: The PR segment is below the TP baseline in the positive leads. Compare a true TP baseline rather than using the displaced PR as zero.

findings.title: Opposite aVR PR and ST changes
findings.explanation: aVR has PR elevation and ST depression. ECG findings support pericarditis only with the history and other diagnostic evidence; use the separate early-repolarization case for comparison.

tca-toxicity.title: Tricyclic / sodium-channel blockade
tca-toxicity.caption: Synthetic educational strip · 6 seconds · selected leads, not a full 12-lead. Grid and waveform share a calibrated scale; on-screen millimetres depend on zoom. Selected morphology, not a clinically validated patient ECG.

findings.title: QRS widening
findings.explanation: The modeled QRS lasts 160 ms. Sodium-channel blocker poisoning is one possible cause of a broad QRS; compare the exposure history and prior ECG.

findings.title: Prominent terminal R in aVR
findings.explanation: The last positive aVR deflection is 4 mm, following a 5 mm S wave (R/S 0.8). A terminal R of at least 3 mm or R/S greater than 0.7 supports this toxic pattern in context.

findings.title: Do not diagnose poisoning from aVR alone
findings.explanation: A terminal aVR R can have other causes. In suspected life-threatening sodium-channel blocker poisoning, urgent toxicology-directed care includes sodium bicarbonate with monitored endpoints.

wpw.title: Wolff–Parkinson–White pre-excitation
wpw.caption: Synthetic educational strip · 6 seconds · selected leads, not a full 12-lead. Grid and waveform share a calibrated scale; on-screen millimetres depend on zoom. Selected morphology, not a clinically validated patient ECG.

findings.title: Short PR to delta onset
findings.explanation: P onset to the first ventricular deflection is 100 ms. Measure PR to the start of the delta wave, not to the steep R upstroke.

findings.title: Delta wave and broad QRS
findings.explanation: The first 40 ms of ventricular activation is slurred; the entire QRS lasts 140 ms. Degree and polarity of pre-excitation vary by lead and accessory pathway.

findings.title: Sinus pattern versus pre-excited AF
findings.explanation: This regular rhythm has organized P waves. WPW pattern does not by itself establish symptomatic WPW syndrome. The separate pre-excited AF example shows a very different irregular tachycardia.

vt-vs-svt.title: Monomorphic ventricular tachycardia
vt-vs-svt.caption: Synthetic focused leads, not a patient recording or a full 12-lead. Each small box represents 40 ms / 0.1 mV at this setting. A regular broad-complex tachycardia should be treated as VT until proved otherwise; seek AV dissociation, capture or fusion beats.

traceSpec.note: A regular broad-complex tachycardia should be treated as VT until proved otherwise; seek AV dissociation, capture or fusion beats.

findings.title: Wide ventricular rhythm
findings.explanation: The underlying rhythm is a broad-complex tachycardia. This teaching model represents VT, not a validated diagnostic algorithm.

findings.title: Capture and fusion examples
findings.explanation: The long strip includes an engineered capture and fusion beat aligned with independent atrial activity. These findings are not present in every VT.

complete-heart-block.title: Complete heart block
complete-heart-block.caption: Synthetic focused leads, not a patient recording or a full 12-lead. Each small box represents 40 ms / 0.1 mV at this setting. Regular P waves march through independently of a slow escape rhythm: complete AV block until proven otherwise.

traceSpec.note: Regular P waves march through independently of a slow escape rhythm: complete AV block until proven otherwise.

findings.title: Independent atrial activity
findings.explanation: P waves continue at their own regular rate, without a fixed relationship to QRS complexes.

findings.title: Slow ventricular escape
findings.explanation: The ventricular rhythm is slower than the atrial rhythm. Inspect the 10-second strip to appreciate AV dissociation.

electrical-alternans.title: Electrical alternans
electrical-alternans.caption: Synthetic educational strip · 6 seconds · selected leads, not a full 12-lead. Grid and waveform share a calibrated scale; on-screen millimetres depend on zoom. Selected morphology, not a clinically validated patient ECG.

findings.title: Alternating QRS amplitude
findings.explanation: Successive QRS complexes alternate between larger and smaller amplitudes while their timing remains regular. Assess several cycles to distinguish alternans from artifact or ectopy.

findings.title: Sinus tachycardia at 110/min
findings.explanation: A P precedes each QRS and the R–R interval is about 545 ms. P and T amplitudes also alternate in this model.

findings.title: Small voltage is not a complete low-voltage diagnosis
findings.explanation: These selected leads have small complexes. Formal low voltage requires assessment of every lead in the relevant limb or precordial set. Alternans does not prove tamponade; assess the patient and obtain echocardiography when indicated.

ischemia-map.caption: Lead and threshold teaching map; not a patient ECG. Voltage examples share the paper scale, but isolated schematic beats do not establish a diagnosis.

findings.title: Inferior ST elevation
findings.explanation: The upper-left example locates the inferior-lead J-point threshold. Apply criteria in contiguous leads and the clinical setting.

findings.title: Reciprocal depression
findings.explanation: The upper-right example shows the opposite ST direction in aVL. Reciprocal changes support interpretation but are not a standalone diagnosis.

findings.title: V2–V3 thresholds
findings.explanation: The middle row separates the sex- and age-specific anterior thresholds. Check the correct category rather than applying 1 mm to every lead.

findings.title: Right-sided and posterior views
findings.explanation: V4R assesses right ventricular involvement; V7–V9 assess the posterior wall. Negative supplemental leads do not exclude occlusion.

findings.title: Other ischemic changes
findings.explanation: The bottom examples locate ST depression, inverted T and a broad/deep Q. Interpret new changes with prior and serial ECGs.

atrial-fibrillation.title: Atrial fibrillation

traceSpec.note: Irregular ventricular response without organized P waves. This example has narrow QRS complexes; it does not model pre-excitation.

atrial-fibrillation.caption: Synthetic focused leads, not a patient recording or a full 12-lead. Each small box represents 40 ms / 0.1 mV at this setting. Irregular ventricular response without organized P waves. This example has narrow QRS complexes; it does not model pre-excitation.

findings.title: Irregular RR intervals
findings.explanation: Successive ventricular intervals genuinely vary in this model; the irregularity is not merely baseline noise.

findings.title: No organized P waves
findings.explanation: Inspect the changing fibrillatory baseline between QRS complexes. There is no repeating sinus P wave or measurable PR interval.

normal-12lead.title: Normal sinus rhythm · full 12-lead
normal-12lead.caption: Synthetic educational 12-lead; not a patient recording. Sequential 2.5-second columns plus a 10-second lead II strip. Swipe inside the paper on phones, or Enlarge to inspect.

findings.title: Sinus rhythm in lead II
findings.explanation: Follow P–QRS–T in lead II. P precedes each QRS with a consistent PR in this synthetic normal rhythm.

findings.title: Compare precordial R progression
findings.explanation: Compare V1 through V6: an initially dominant S gives way to larger R waves. The columns show sequential time windows, not simultaneous beats.

findings.title: Ten-second rhythm strip
findings.explanation: Use the continuous bottom lead II to assess regularity over time. The upper columns each cover 2.5 seconds.

findings.title: Calibration pulse
findings.explanation: The pulse at the left of the rhythm strip represents 1 mV and 200 ms. Check gain and speed before making measurements.
